name: ULN2003 Darlington Array
summary: Seven open-collector Darlington sinks with built-in clamp diodes, for relays, solenoids and 28BYJ-48 steppers.
logic: Inputs 5 V TTL, outputs to 50 V
notes: Outputs sink only. The load goes between your positive rail and the output pin, never between the output and ground. Getting this backwards is why nothing switches on.
Pin 9 is COM, the common cathode of the flyback diodes. Tie it to the load's positive rail or the diodes do nothing and inductive kick goes through the chip instead.
The output order is reversed against the inputs: IN1 on pin 1 drives OUT1 on pin 16, IN2 on pin 2 drives OUT2 on pin 15, and so on down to IN7 and OUT7 on pins 7 and 10.
500 mA per channel, but not on all seven at once. The package dissipation limit lands around 1.5 W total, so a full load of seven relays will overheat it.
Darlington saturation drop is about 1 V at 350 mA, wasted as heat. The TBD62083A is pin compatible, DMOS, and drops a third of a volt.
ULN2003 inputs are sized for 5 V logic. ULN2004 is the same part with input resistors for 6 to 15 V CMOS.
For eight channels use the ULN2803, which is DIP-18 with a different pinout rather than a wider version of this one.

pins.name: COM
pins.note: Connect to the load's supply rail. Without it the clamp diodes are not in circuit.

pins.name: OUT1
pins.note: Driven by IN1 on pin 1, at the opposite corner.
